newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan March kerosene imports seen falling sharply.
newsitem.headline: Japan March kerosene imports seen falling sharply.

text.p: Japan's kerosene imports next month are expected to fall sharply from last March as high stockpiles continue to meet languishing demand, traders said on Wednesday.
"Our kerosene imports in March are expected to be less than half the volume we imported last year," a trader with a refiner said.
"Sales are poor and domestic supplies sufficient while domestic refinery operating rates are around the same levels as last year," he said.
In January, imports of kerosene, used to heat households, fell by 11.1 percent to 619,000 kilolitres (kl), according to the latest Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) statistics.
Imports boomed during the winter of 1995/96 as refiners were caught short of supplies on the back of unexpectedly cold temperatures which lasted up to April.
In March 1996, Japan imported 778,000 kl of kerosene, according to MITI data.
In contrast, stockpiles of kerosene grew this winter because of mild temperatures, traders said.
Kerosene inventories held by refineries, distributors and importers as of end-January were 3.4 million kilolitres (kl), up 30.2 percent from a year earlier, according to MITI.
"End-January stockpiles increased even though January sales were quite good," a second trader with a separate refiner said.
Sales in January were 4.8 million kl, up 6.9 percent from the previous year, the first year-on-year increase in three months, the MITI data showed.
Traders said some consumers bought supplies in January, ahead of a hefty price hike in February wholesale prices.
Major refiners raised their kerosene wholesale prices for February by about 1,200 yen per kl from January, to around 38,500 yen per kl.
"Warm temperatures and the hurried buying in January is weighing on February sales," the second trader said.

Temperatures in Sapporo, in Japan's northern island of Hokkaido, averaged minus 2.1 degrees Celsius in the second 10 days of February, against normal levels for the period of minus 4.4 degrees C, according to the local weather agency.
In Sapporo, where kerosene is heavily consumed, March temperatures are forecast to be higher than normal, the agency said.
Japan's kerosene demand is highest during November to March, peaking in February.
